Use case: identity-preserve / stylized-concept.
Asset type: production sprite animation sheet for Elías, a top-down 2D pixel-art RPG hero.
Reference 1 is the APPROVED full-body pixel-art model and defines the exact anatomy, proportions, face, hair, clothing and rendering. Reference 2 is the original costume design. Keep the beautiful compact anatomy of reference 1, about 3.5 heads tall. Fully redraw every pose as one coherent figure, never make a cutout puppet or stretch/rotate disjoint limbs.
Elías: young adult man, blond tousled hair, green eyes, forest-green sleeveless vest, cream rolled-sleeve shirt, brown diagonal baldric and belts, burgundy sash, charcoal trousers, dark leather boots. A short straight sword remains SHEATHED on anatomical LEFT hip. No cape, no armor, no drawn weapon.
Style: clean intentional JRPG pixel art. Strong compact clusters and dark outlines, limited consistent earthy palette, subtle top-down RPG view, same scale and lighting in every frame. All eight figures must have the SAME head size, torso volume, thigh length, shin length, hand and boot size.
Sheet format: landscape TRANSPARENT background, precisely FOUR equally spaced columns and TWO equally spaced rows. Exactly EIGHT whole characters, one in each equal cell. Read in row-major order. Each figure fits fully in its own cell with clear empty gutters. Constant ground baseline and consistent body scale. No text, numbers, borders, diagrams, motion lines, scenery, dust, duplicates or shadows. These eight frames must form a smooth loop with clearly different limb positions.
Animation: RUN RIGHT / EAST, exactly eight sequential frames. Every face points to the RIGHT throughout, full side profile with a slight top-down view. The sword is on the FAR hip in this direction, mostly obscured by the body.
The torso leans forward gently, ~10 degrees, but stays a solid, balanced volume. Elbows are bent near 90 degrees; arms pump opposite to their respective legs. Knees bend naturally, never backwards. Feet and hands are compact. Use a NORMAL comfortable running stride, NOT exaggerated splits, NOT rubber limbs.
Frame 1: near leg reaches forward to contact, far leg folds behind; near elbow back, far fist forward.
Frame 2: weight compresses over near foot, near knee bends modestly; far knee passes underneath pelvis.
Frame 3: near foot pushes off behind hip, far knee comes forward high; near arm begins forward swing.
Frame 4: short flight, far thigh reaches ahead, near heel curls toward the back, both feet clear the ground.
Frame 5: opposite contact, FAR leg ahead, NEAR leg behind, arm swing reverses.
Frame 6: weight compresses over FAR foot, NEAR knee passes underneath pelvis.
Frame 7: FAR foot pushes back; NEAR knee comes forward high, FAR arm swings forward.
Frame 8: short flight with NEAR thigh ahead, FAR heel curled behind, smoothly leading back to frame 1.
Keep hip height on a gentle repeating down/up arc, and draw full natural anatomy and connected clothing in ALL frames. No long straight stilts for legs. Both halves of the gait must be present.
